resources.string: Voltage, current, charge times and a 24 hour graph
The graph fills in as you use the console. A point is added every 15 minutes while it is awake.
Printed on the battery. Wrong values make the percentage drift.
Finds out how much the battery really holds: one full charge, then play until the console turns off

This finds out how much charge the battery really holds, so the percentage gets more accurate.

1. Charge until the console says full.
2. Unplug and use the console as usual until it turns off by itself. Sleep and restarts are fine, but don't charge in between.
3. Charge it and turn it on again. The result shows up here.

A notification shows how far it is.
The charge limit is on, so the battery never gets full. Turn the charge limit off first.
Waiting: charge until full, then unplug
Full. Unplug the charger to start
%1$d mAh used so far. Keep going until the console turns off.
Stop measuring? What was counted so far is lost.
The battery holds about %1$d mAh. Tap to use it.
The battery gave %1$d mAh from full until the console turned off. Use %2$d mAh as its capacity?
Stopped: the charger went in before the battery was empty. Tap to try again.
Stopped: the console was charged before the battery was empty. Tap to try again.
Stopped: the count came out too low to be right. Tap to try again.
Off. For a console that stays on the charger, a limit makes the battery last more years.
Stops charging at %1$d%% and starts again at %2$d%%. The console runs from the charger in between. Turn it off before a long trip to get a full charge.
Plugged in, held at the charge limit

The percentage is the fuel gauge's estimate. The voltage is measured directly: about 4.2 V is full, 3.7 V is around the middle and the console turns off near 3.4 V. Voltage drops while a game is running and recovers at rest.

If the percentage and the voltage don't match, charge until the console says full. That lets the gauge correct itself.

Times are rough guesses from the current right now.
